say.en: On the due date Bimal's shop has had a poor season and he cannot pay. The bill is dishonoured. What does Asha do, who pays the notary, and can the debt be given more time? In this lesson: Record the dishonour of a bill retained, discounted or endorsed.
Treat noting charges.

body.en: A bill is dishonoured when the drawee does not pay it on the due date. To have legal proof, the holder may get it noted by a notary public, who charges a fee called noting charges. These are finally borne by the drawee, since the *dishonour* is his fault. On dishonour the drawee again becomes a debtor of the drawer for the amount of the bill plus noting charges. In the drawer's books the credit goes to Bills Receivable if she still held the bill, to Bank if it had been discounted, or to the endorsee if it had been endorsed.

points.en: Retained: Drawee A/c Dr, To Bills Receivable A/c, To Cash A/c (*noting*)
Discounted: Drawee A/c Dr, To Bank A/c (amount + *noting*)
Endorsed: Drawee A/c Dr, To Endorsee A/c (amount + *noting*)
Drawee: Bills Payable A/c Dr, *Noting* Charges A/c Dr, To Drawer A/c

Retained: Drawee A over c Dr, To Bills Receivable A over c, To Cash A over c noting.
Discounted: Drawee A over c Dr, To Bank A over c amount plus noting.
Endorsed: Drawee A over c Dr, To Endorsee A over c amount plus noting.
Drawee: Bills Payable A over c Dr, Noting Charges A over c Dr, To Drawer A over c.

body.en: If the drawee knows in advance that he cannot pay, he may ask the drawer to cancel the old bill and accept a new one for a longer period. The drawer charges interest for the extra time on the amount still due. Three steps follow in each book: cancel the old bill, charge (or bear) the interest, and record the new bill. Interest may be paid in cash or added to the amount of the new bill.

points.en: Cancel: Drawee A/c Dr, To *Bills* Receivable A/c
Interest: Drawee A/c Dr, To Interest A/c
New bill: *Bills* Receivable A/c Dr, To Drawee A/c

steps.en: Record the bill received: Bills Receivable A/c Dr, To Drawee A/c
On dishonour: Drawee A/c Dr, To Bills Receivable A/c and To Cash A/c (noting charges)
Charge interest for the extra period: Drawee A/c Dr, To Interest A/c
Receive the new accepted bill: Bills Receivable A/c Dr, To Drawee A/c
On the new due date: Bank A/c Dr, To Bills Receivable A/c

explanation.en: Dishonour revives the drawee's debt; interest is added for the extra time; the new bill replaces the debt and is met on its own due date.

problem.en: Hari's acceptance of ₹20,000, held by Sita till maturity, is dishonoured; noting charges are ₹100. Hari pays ₹5,100 in cash and accepts a new 2-month bill for the balance with interest at 12% p.a. Find the amount of the new bill.

steps.en: After the cash payment the balance is 20,100 − 5,100 = ₹15,000.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Hari's acceptance of ₹20,000, held by Sita till maturity, is dishonoured; noting charges are ₹100. Hari pays ₹5,100 in cash and accepts a new 2-month bill for the balance with interest at 12% p.a. Find the amount of the new bill.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Hari's acceptance of 20,000, rupees held by Sita till maturity, is dishonoured; noting charges are 100 rupees. Hari pays 5,100 rupees in cash and accepts a new 2-month bill for the balance with interest at 12 percent p.a. Find the amount of the new bill.
On dishonour Hari owes 20,000 plus 100 equals 20,100 rupees.
After the cash payment the balance is 20,100 minus 5,100 equals 15,000 rupees.
Interest equals 15,000 times 12 over 100 times 2 over 12 equals 300 rupees.
New bill equals 15,000 plus 300 equals 15,300 rupees.
So the answer is The new bill is for 15,300 rupees.

heading.en: Credit the account that lost the money

body.en: On dishonour, always debit the drawee. Credit whoever is out of pocket: Bills Receivable (if held), Bank (if discounted) or the endorsee (if endorsed). Noting charges go with the amount.
